author.role: Implementation author preparing a future prerequisite proposal; not an independent review of authored source

context_at_creation.current_own_C_success: Root-reported controlled returned-process evidence: current own PID pidfd open, matching proc/fdinfo PID, poll0, once-close, F_GETFD/EBADF; independent actual audit pending at proposal creation
context_at_creation.current_proof_limit: Own-PID operations and narrow C-runtime boundary only; no child creation, controller-loss cleanup, full containment, model-runtime ABI, physical resource lease or foreign restoration

minimum_increment.objective: Observe one fixed owned direct worker child under a separate owned C guard, including normal lifecycle and deliberately induced loss of a separately owned controller; retain actual identities, wait/poll and cleanup outcomes
minimum_increment.process_layout_proposal: A fresh bounded observation coordinator directly owns one fixed controller and one fixed guard; the guard directly owns one fixed worker. Maximum four fresh processes including the coordinator, with no services or additional descendants. Every PID comes from this new fixture's own fork results/private handshake, never a free PID input.
minimum_increment.normal_case: Private inherited pipe handshakes bind all owned roles before the fixed worker may proceed. Observe worker readiness/progress, request fixed orderly completion, match its waitpid status, close each owned pidfd once and verify descriptor closure without reusing process identifiers.
minimum_increment.controller_loss_case: After all ownership handshakes, the dedicated owned controller deliberately exits through its reviewed fixed fixture path. The surviving guard observes that exact controller pidfd become readable, rechecks its own/direct-worker identity and signals only its verified live direct worker through the reviewed symbolic pidfd interface. Record worker pidfd exit, the matching waitpid termination status and the coordinator's matching controller/guard exit observations.
minimum_increment.episode_separation: Normal and controller-loss cases require separately declared fresh scopes/case identities, nonce/paths/attempts and one execution each after their source and exact-prelaunch gates. This proposal chooses no nonce, request, argv, source closure or output path.
minimum_increment.implementation_size_limit: One fixed C product and the smallest separate observation/parser/fixture interface needed for those two cases; no model bridge, production launcher or general process-management API
minimum_increment.design_choice_not_frozen: Process layout, coordinator implementation and evidence interfaces require an independent design review before source work; reported cleanup cannot substitute for independently observed exit facts.

future_source_requirements: New operational source closure on a normal branch from latest actual integrated main after current result integration; preserve all current and historical source/data/receipt bytes

Review the declared C syscall signature and actual captured SYS_pidfd_open/SYS_pidfd_send_signal, SIGKILL, poll, waitpid and fork/pipe constants and interfaces through system headers; no guessed number/provider/architecture and no reuse of the current linked product
Fresh compiler/header/CPP/object/link/product/interpreter bindings; existing trusted baseline remains explicit rather than claiming complete compiler, loader or mapped-code authentication

Private inherited handshakes and role-bound nonce; exact fresh boot, UID/EUID, PID, PPID, birth/start identity and controller/guard/worker ownership facts. Guard must own its direct child and reject identity/source/clock drift before permitting work or signal.

Acquire and bind fresh pidfds only for the fixture's newly created processes. Preserve first failure plus acquired-FD, signal-attempt, close, wait/reap and unknown-outcome facts; never signal a PID merely because its numeric value matches.

Bound every phase with reviewed monotonic finite deadlines, work and cleanup budgets appropriate to the tiny CPU fixture. No retry on failed signal/close, no indefinite waits, and no complete cleanup promise on host loss or async interruption.

Minimal fixed worker CPU action only. No executable/path/command/PID/flag supplied by an external request; any normal/loss case selector must be a closed reviewed fixture enum and must not unlock general --execute.

A separately reviewed observation interface must verify PID-birth/handshake binding and kernel poll/wait outcomes without relying only on guard success booleans. Controller/guard exit observed by their own coordinator is not an independent proof of every worker cleanup edge.
Keep old Python os API, old native _require_linux guard, saved CLI refusal and scientific/native implementations untouched; new C functionality cannot shim old APIs or release production execution.
Independent source/committed/saved-CI reviews, commit/push, attached PR, all latest exact-head Python3.10/3.14 push+PR CI successes and actual main integration precede any new host phase.
meaningful_future_CPU_fixtures: Portable parser negatives for foreign PID/PPID/UID/boot/birth/nonce/source, duplicate/nonfinite JSON, forged success, wrong waitpid identity/status, stale descriptor, missing readiness and inconsistent cleanup facts
A real Linux fixed normal direct-child fixture with matched ownership handshake, bounded progress, expected orderly exit and exactly scoped descriptor close/reap facts

A real Linux fresh controlled controller-loss fixture with surviving guard, exact controller pidfd exit, actual owned-worker termination and matched waitpid facts; an injected ready boolean is insufficient

Deterministic boundary tests for prelaunch expiry, clock reverse/nonfinite, source/identity drift and controller loss around handshakes; preserve actual failure classification rather than masking it with elapsed time
Timeout/cleanup error or unknown outcomes remain negative/partial and consumed; unsupported headers/runtime fail after declared Linux prerequisites rather than being reported as capability success
No current or historical tests, host observations, probes, controllers, raw retrievals or exclusive output paths are rerun by this proposal.
future_host_requirements: Only after all new source gates, declare exact inputs/dispatcher and independently accepted exact-prelaunch review with a new scope/case/nonce/root/attempt; no reuse or fallback from PR40's consumed host episode
Read MS skills before actual SSH and remain within N1-1/N1-3/N4-1..4; CPU-only phase with no GPU occupancy scan, CUDA initialization, model, installation or foreign queue action
Retain original bootstrap as an input expectation checked freshly, never substitute an interpreter to retry a consumed episode

Returned controlled-process evidence and raw caller streams must be preserved without claiming independent remote retrieval, full ancestry/node-alias authentication, physical exclusion, persistence or host-loss cleanup.

acceptance_boundary.possible_future_narrow_claim: Only the particular separately declared fixed owned direct-child lifecycle and controlled controller-loss cleanup case, with its independently reviewed actual facts

immutable_boundaries.future_GPU_model_stage: Separate integrated model/native bridge and owned controller/guard, fresh full runtime/data/weights checks, live lease and independently verified full original-queue restore remain prerequisites; 4500s work +1500s recovery is not supplied by this tiny fixture.
